name: Hiwatt DR103 Custom 100 (1970 Partridge)
description: Hiwatt DR103 Custom 100: Partridge-era four-input preamp (two channels, shared V1 cathode), V2 mixer pair with a common 100 kOhm plate load, the Hiwatt TMB tone stack, a 220 kOhm Master Volume, V3a recovery and V3b fixed-bias cathode-follower reference, the Hiwatt fixed-bias long-tailed-pair phase inverter (82 kOhm/91 kOhm plates, 22 kOhm tail, 10 kOhm feedback from the 16 Ohm tap, 1 nF/100 kOhm/470 Ohm/100 nF/470 Ohm/10 nF presence network), and four EL34s in parallel push-pull with 22 kOhm grid stoppers, 100 kOhm grid leaks to a -38 V bias rail, 100 Ohm screen stoppers from a 470 Ohm screen bus, and a Partridge TH7549/2 output transformer (Raa 1750 Ohm, 16/8/4 Ohm taps, feedback from the 16 Ohm tap) into a 16 Ohm Hiwatt SE4123-class cab. Supply: Partridge TH7548/5-class PT (350 VAC HT, 50 VAC bias) into a 1N5408 bridge, a 2x220 uF/350 V series reservoir, standby, 100 Ohm 5 W to the screen feed, 470 Ohm 10 W to the screen bus, 1 kOhm to HT3, a 2x50 uF/450 V + 220 uF/350 V series HT3 filter with 220 kOhm balancing, and a -38 V bias supply. Mains 230 Vrms 50 Hz.

sources.title: Hiwatt DR103 Preamp Circuit Diagram, factory sheet, drawn 19/05/95 Issue 4, S/No. AB0309 onwards (Audio Brothers/Biacrown owners manual): V1-V4 = ECC83, 220k plate loads, shared 1k5/100uF V1 cathode, 100k V2 common plate load, 1k cathodes with one 47n bypass, Hiwatt TMB stack values, 220k master, 100k/1k5 V3a, 100k/1M/220k V3b reference, 82k/91k PI, 22k tail, 2k2, 10k feedback, 100k presence + 100n + 470R + 10n

Hiwatt DR103 Output Stage Circuit Diagram, factory sheet, drawn 25/04/94 Issue 1: four EL34, 22k grid stoppers, 100k grid leaks to BIAS, 100R screen stoppers, 470R 10W screen feed from H.T. SUPPLY 2, Partridge TH7549/2 with 16/8/4 Ohm taps and a feedback terminal

Hiwatt DR103 Power Supply Circuit Diagram, factory sheet, drawn 22/11/94 Issue 3: Partridge TH7548/5, 1N5408 bridge, 2x220 uF/350 V reservoir with 220k balancing, 100R 5W, 470R 10W, 1k 1W, 2x50 uF/450 V + 220 uF/350 V stack, 220k/220k balance, 1k/1N5408/100uF/47k bias to -38 V

Mark Huss, Hiwatt 100 W Output Stage drawing v1.1 and 100 W Power Supply drawing v1.3 (Partridge TG7549/TH7549, TG9302/TH7548, 460 V HT1, -38 V bias), and Mid-70s Four-Input Preamp drawing rev 1.4 (Hiwatt TMB stack, 220k master, V3a/V3b, fixed-bias PI)

Richard Kuehnel, Amp Books, 'Hiwatt Fixed-Bias Phase Inverter': cathode-follower reference 1M/220k and 220k cathode, LTP grids at 73 V through 100k and 1M, 22k tail, 10k feedback in parallel with 2.2k, 82k/91k plates, presence network 1n/100k/470R/100n plus fixed 470R/10n

Mark Huss, Hiwatt technical page: DR103 Partridge output transformer primary impedance 1750 Ohm, -3 dB 3.6 Hz to 112 kHz; DR103 power transformer 350 VAC @ 300 mA HT, 50 VAC @ 50 mA bias; DR201 Partridge primary DCR about 36 Ohm; classic valve line-up V1-V3 ECC83, V4 ECC81

parts.label: HT secondary half (350 Vrms, 495 V peak), phase A
parts.note: The DR103 uses a 1N5408 bridge on one 350 VAC winding; a floating winding cannot be expressed with ground-referenced V sources, so the bridge is modelled as the equivalent two-diode full-wave from anti-phase sources of the full-winding peak (the JCM800/5E3 convention). One diode drop instead of two.

parts.note: Presence 100 k lin. Lugs (fixed 2026-11-11, control audit): the factory sheet does not number the lugs; the clockwise end is the 100 nF / feedback-junction side (prb), as the Amp Books Hiwatt PI analysis states (wiper fully right = 470 R against the 0.1 uF = treble boost) and the owner manual requires (presence gives an extremely bright sound at the upper end). It was wired the other way round, so up removed highs (-15.5 dB at 8 kHz).

Bias supply filter node (-38 V)
parts.note: The factory PSU sheet prints -38 V after the 1k / 1N5408 / 100 uF 63 V / 47 k bias rectifier off the 50 VAC bias winding. Modelled as the printed filter node, as the JCM800/Plexi/AB763 netlists do, because a negative-peak rectifier is not charged at the mains-crest operating point used by --settle 0. The real network is in the notes.
